newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nanjing retailer to seek Hong Kong listing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nanjing retailer to seek Hong Kong listing - paper.

text.p: Nanjing Central Emporium Stock is seeking to become the first Chinese retailer to list its shares overseas, aiming at a flotation in Hong Kong in 1997, the South China Morning Post reported on Wednesday.

The daily quoted the Nanjing municipal government-backed emporium's general manager Lu Guangling as saying Nanjing Central had applied to securities regulators to be included in the fourth batch of companies allowed to issue shares abroad.
Proceeds from the listing will be used to expand the company's supermarket chain and develop an industrial park for product processing and assembly, Lu said.
Last year, the emporium's turnover grew 34 percent to 1.25 billion yuan with net profit exceeding 30 million yuan, Lu said.
The department stores has 18 supermarkets and plans to increase to 30 by the end of 1996 and to 200 within five years, the Morning Post said.
